ken: Kicking off a targeted bring-up for sundial-int6 (6-bit per-channel prototype). Running against conch-emb-512 fp16 baseline on wiki/product holdouts. CI job: https://ci.internal/8421
maria: Nice. What config are you using? batch/seq/seed/holdout?
ken: CI config in job notes: batch=128, seq=256, seed=777, holdout=wiki_holdout_30k.json. Metrics: recall@1/10/100, silhouette, jaccard_top10, PCA variance.
sam: First pass finished  looks like recall@10 is down ~3.9% vs baseline on 30k.
ci-bot: Job 8421 completed  FAILED (recall regression > 2%). Details: baseline recall@10=0.821, sundial-int6=0.789.
maria: Any stratification by query length or label?
ken: Short queries (<7 tokens) take the biggest hit: recall@1 down ~6.5%. Medium queries down ~3.0%, long nearly flat.
jules: Could be per-dim clipping or scale mismatch. Did you check L2-norm distributions pre/post quant?
ken: Yes  mean L2 norm drops ~8% after quant. Also first-32 PCA variance drops noticeably.
sam: Do we have qualitative id-flips to inspect?
ken: Pasting a few short-query flips (trimmed):
1) Query: "install docker"  baseline top1: doc#412 (install steps) sim=0.90, sundial top1: doc#789 (docker internals) sim=0.66
2) Query: "oauth refresh token"  baseline top1: doc#1201 (refresh flow) sim=0.88, sundial top1: doc#3210 (jwt rotate) sim=0.60
3) Query: "merge branches"  baseline top1: doc#23 (merge vs rebase) sim=0.86, sundial top1: doc#88 (stash/merge) sim=0.62
maria: Thanks. Hypothesis: per-channel outliers getting clipped or asymmetric distribution causing bias. Options: percentile clipping (0.999), tiny affine calibration before quant, or light distillation.
ken: I'll run three follow-ups: (A) per-channel percentile clip int6 (job 8422), (B) affine-calib pre-quant (job 8423), (C) distillation on 250k pairs for 3k steps (job 8424). Launching now.
ci-bot: Jobs queued: 8422 ETA 1h30m, 8423 ETA 1h50m, 8424 ETA 3h.
sam: Also compute Jaccard(top10) vs baseline by length bucket (<7, 7-25, >25) and save top-50 id-flip examples per run.
jules: If clipping doesn't help, consider hybrid: keep top-8 dims in higher precision or retrain student with L2-normalization loss before quant.
ken: Agreed. I'll include PCA variance plots, per-length recall curves, and sample failure dump in follow-ups. Will update when jobs finish. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
